summary:
Oops! I'm an Astronaut is an interactive 3D educational adventure game that lets students experience the challenges of exploring and living beyond Earth. Players take on the role of an astronaut, explore Moon and Mars environments, complete four structured missions, manage resources, construct habitats, work with greenhouse systems, and conduct research.

The game combines interactive gameplay with scientific context from NASA resources, including DONKI, OSDR, RadLab, and Mars Trek. It clearly distinguishes real scientific information from simulated gameplay systems, helping players understand space exploration without confusing simulations with actual astronaut measurements.

By turning space science into an engaging, mission-based experience, the game aims to make learning more interactive and inspire the next generation of space explorers.
details:
Oops! I'm an Astronaut

Project Overview

Oops! I'm an Astronaut is an interactive 3D educational space exploration game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer."

The game transforms traditional space learning into an immersive adventure where students take on the role of an astronaut and experience the challenges of exploring and preparing for life beyond Earth.

How It Works

Players explore two extraterrestrial environments: the Moon and Mars. Through four structured missions, they progress through different aspects of astronaut exploration:

  1. Begin the Journey – Get introduced to the astronaut experience and mission objectives.
  2. Explore and Survive – Explore planetary environments and learn about survival challenges.
  3. Build and Prepare – Manage resources and construct essential structures, including habitats and greenhouse systems.
  4. Research and Discover – Engage with research activities and scientific exploration.

The game combines third-person exploration, interactive objectives, resource management, construction, research mechanics, and mission progression. Tutorial guidance and save/resume functionality help players navigate and continue their experience.

GitHub Link:

https://github.com/Ashfaq-Developer-2011/Junior-Astronaut-Mission-Trainer-

NASA Data and Scientific Integration

A key feature of the game is its integration of NASA scientific resources:

  • NASA DONKI: Provides space weather event information and context for understanding solar activity.
  • NASA OSDR: Provides access to spaceflight research metadata.
  • NASA RadLab: Provides radiation research context relevant to human space exploration.
  • NASA Mars Trek: Provides Mars imagery and terrain context.
  • Habitat Demonstration Unit(HDU): Used as a reference for NASA habitat concepts and human exploration habitat design.
  • NASA Central Public API: Used to access NASA's publicly available APIs and related space-science information.
  • NASA Apollo Lunar Module (Lander): Used as a visual and educational reference for lunar landing vehicle design, helping represent the technology used during historic Moon missions.

The game uses a backend proxy to retrieve relevant resources, with caching and fallback content to maintain availability.

Scientific accuracy is an important consideration. Real NASA observations and research information are distinguished from simulated gameplay values. Research data is not presented as direct personal astronaut measurements, and procedural terrain is not claimed to be scientifically measured elevation data.

Technology and Development

The game was developed using:

  • React 19 and TypeScript – Frontend application and game logic.
  • Three.js – 3D rendering and environments.
  • React Three Fiber and Drei – Integration of 3D scenes into React.
  • Vite – Development and production build tooling.
  • Tailwind CSS – Interface styling.
  • Express.js – Backend services and NASA data proxy routes.
  • IndexedDB and localStorage – Save/resume functionality and local persistence.
  • Web Audio API – Gameplay sound effects.

The game is deployed publicly through Vercel.

Creativity and Innovation

Instead of presenting astronaut training as a collection of facts, Oops! I'm an Astronaut turns space exploration concepts into an interactive learning experience.

Players do not simply read about extraterrestrial environments; they explore them, complete mission objectives, manage resources, construct structures, and engage with research activities.

The combination of two planetary environments, structured missions, interactive 3D gameplay, and NASA scientific resources creates a unified educational experience.

. What does it do or how does it work?

Oops! I'm an Astronaut is an interactive educational game that lets players experience the challenges of being an astronaut. Players take on different space missions, complete challenges, answer questions, and learn about the science behind human space exploration. The game uses real NASA data to make the learning experience more meaningful and scientifically grounded. Instead of simply reading about space, players learn by exploring, making decisions, and completing missions.

2. What benefits does it have?

The game makes learning about space more engaging, interactive, and accessible, especially for students and young learners. It helps players understand astronaut activities, space science, and the challenges of human space exploration through gameplay. It also encourages curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and interest in STEM education.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our goal is to make space education more exciting and accessible to everyone. We want students to develop an interest in science and space exploration without feeling that learning is complicated or boring. By combining gaming with authentic NASA information, we hope to inspire the next generation of space enthusiasts, scientists, and explorers.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

We used AI-assisted development tools to design and build the game.

  • Google AI Studio (Build Mode): AI-assisted application development.
  • Stitch: Designing and planning the user interface.
  • NASA Open Data and APIs: Accessing real scientific information, including relevant NASA DONKI, OSDR, and RADLab data.
  • Web technologies: Frontend development and interactive game functionality.
  • AI tools: Supporting development, debugging, design, and project documentation.

The project was developed as a web-based game, so no specialized physical hardware was required.

5. How is your project creative?

Our creativity comes from turning space science into an interactive gaming experience. Rather than presenting NASA information through traditional lessons or dashboards, we allow players to experience astronaut-related challenges themselves. We combine gameplay, missions, interactive elements, and real NASA data to create an experience that is both entertaining and educational. The idea is simple: make players feel like they are learning through an adventure rather than studying a textbook.

6. What factors did your team consider?

While developing the game, we considered several important factors:

  • Scientific accuracy: Using authentic NASA information wherever applicable.
  • Educational value: Making sure players actually learn something through gameplay.
  • User experience: Keeping navigation and gameplay simple and understandable.
  • Target audience: Designing an experience suitable for students and young learners.
  • Engagement: Making missions interactive, enjoyable, and rewarding.
  • Accessibility: Making the game accessible through a web browser.
  • Technical feasibility: Building a functional experience within the limited hackathon timeframe.

Factors Considered

During development, the team considered:

  • Scientific credibility and responsible use of NASA data.
  • Age-appropriate and accessible learning experiences for students.
  • Clear mission progression and intuitive controls.
  • Distinguishing real scientific information from simulated gameplay.
  • Reliable NASA data retrieval and offline fallback behavior.
  • Game performance, responsiveness, and player progression.
  • A balance between educational value and engaging gameplay.

Intended Impact

The goal is to make space science more accessible, interactive, and exciting for students.

By introducing planetary exploration, astronaut challenges, resource management, and scientific research through gameplay, the experience aims to encourage curiosity, critical thinking, and interest in science, technology, engineering, and space exploration.

Oops! I'm an Astronaut — Explore. Learn. Make Mistakes. Discover.

Developed by Team LONE WOLVES for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

AI Tools and Assisted Development (Si Super Intelligence)

Artificial Intelligence tools were used as development assistants to accelerate implementation, improve productivity, and support the creation of the game's presentation materials.

The tools used included:

  • Google AI Studio: AI-assisted application development, code generation, implementation, debugging, and refinement of game features.
  • ChatGPT: Prompt engineering, technical planning, development guidance, debugging assistance, documentation, scientific explanations, and content preparation.
  • Canva AI: Assisted in creating presentation materials, visual communication assets, and promotional content.
  • Gamma AI: Assisted in generating presentation layouts and organizing project information into a visual pitch.
  • HIX AI: Assisted in generating cinematic promotional video content.
  • Stitch: Assisted in designing and exploring the game's user interface concepts.

AI tools supported the development process, but the game concept, feature selection, project direction, integration decisions, and final implementation were managed by the team.

NASA scientific resources were used as the source of scientific context rather than treating AI-generated information as scientific observations.

AI-assisted and AI-generated content is acknowledged appropriately, and generated visual or audio assets are identified according to the competition's disclosure requirements.
